items.body:
<details open>

tests : qualify isnan and signbit with std:: (#31791)

* tests : qualify isnan and signbit with std::

The unqualified calls rely on the C math.h names also being present in the
global namespace, which is not the case for the NetBSD 11.99.9/x86_64 gcc
14.4.0 build reported in the issue.  Prefix the calls with std:: to select
the standard C++ overloads declared by <cmath>.

ref: https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/issues/1681

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB)

* tests : qualify C math calls with std::

Follow-up to the isnan / signbit fix: make the remaining math calls in
test-quantize-fns.cpp consistent with the std:: isfinite / max / numeric_limits
already used in the same file.

The float variants are overloads in C++, not distinct names, so the mapping is
fabsf -> std::fabs, copysignf -> std::copysign, nextafterf -> std::nextafter -
not std::fabsf & friends, which do not exist in libstdc++ and would break the
gcc build.  NAN and INFINITY are macros and are left unqualified.

Only behavioural difference: array_rmse() fed a double accumulator to sqrtf(),
now std::sqrt() keeps the computation in double.  The result is more accurate
and differs from the previous value by at most 1.4e-7 relative, three orders of
magnitude below the tightest tolerance in this test.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB)

</details>

<details open>

tests : override hardware_concurrency in CI (#31797)

The self-hosted CPU runners are containers with 8 CPUs, but
std::thread::hardware_concurrency reports the cores of the host. The
table mode of test-llama-context sizes its pool from that count, so it
runs 4 models x 8 threads on an 8-CPU job and hangs.

Add TEST_ARG_HARDWARE_CONCURRENCY and TEST_ARG_PARALLEL_WORKERS as the
defaults for the auto-selected counts of test-llama-context and of
test-backend-ops, and set them to 8 and 4 for cpu-x64-high-perf.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB)

</details>
